days.title: Before you start
days.brief: Hi! I'm May. This week you're going to say your first English sentences out loud. They don't have to be perfect: they just have to come out. Today we only get ready.
days.why: What holds a beginner back most isn't grammar: it's the fear of opening your mouth. That's why we start by recording you exactly as you are today.
days.challenge: Say out loud: "Hi, I'm …". Just that. You've started.

steps.text: Book your first call with Mei (25 minutes).
Record your Day 1: read the card out loud, even if it comes out badly.
Write down three reasons you want to speak English.
Add the week to your calendar: 20 minutes a day.

days.title: Me
days.goal: Say five true sentences about yourself, without reading.
days.brief: Today you talk about yourself. Your name, where you're from, what you do, what you like. These are the sentences you'll use in every conversation of your life.
days.why: Introducing yourself without reading is the first win. Once it comes out on its own, the rest of the conversation stops being so scary.
days.challenge: Introduce yourself out loud in front of the mirror, five sentences, without looking at your phone.
days.mistakeWhy: You don't use "have" for age: in English you are your years.
phrases: Me gustan la música y el fútbol.
I'm learning English because I want to travel.
Estoy aprendiendo inglés porque quiero viajar.
freeze: My English is not very good, but I'm learning.
Mi inglés no es muy bueno, pero estoy aprendiendo.

days.title: Order and ask
days.can: I can order food and drink.
days.goal: Order a drink and something to eat, and pay.
days.brief: Today you ask for things: a coffee, something to eat, the bill. In English, asking with "I'd like" and "Can I have" sounds polite and natural.
days.why: Ordering is the most common real situation when you travel. If you can order, you can get by on your own.
days.challenge: Order today's breakfast in English, out loud, even if you're at home.
days.mistakeWhy: "Give me a coffee" sounds rude in English. Use "Can I have…?" or "I'd like…".
phrases: Can I have a sandwich, please?
Can I pay by card, please?

days.title: Questions
days.can: I can ask for what I need.
days.goal: Ask where, what time and how, and ask for something politely.
days.brief: Today you ask questions: where something is, what time something leaves, how to get there. A good question saves you anywhere.
days.why: Whoever asks the questions leads the conversation. And when you don't understand the answer, you'll know what to say too.
days.challenge: Ask someone (or your pet) three questions in English. What matters is saying them.
days.mistakeWhy: In questions the verb comes first: "Where is the bathroom?", not "Where the bathroom is?".
phrases: Could I have a window seat, please?
¿Me podría dar un asiento de ventana, por favor?
How do I get to the station?
freeze: Can you show me on the map?
¿Me lo puedes enseñar en el mapa?
¿A la izquierda o a la derecha?

days.title: Yesterday
days.can: I can say what I did.
days.goal: Say three things you did yesterday and how it was.
days.brief: Today you tell what you did yesterday. The past looks hard, but with ten verbs you can already tell almost anything.
days.why: Telling your day is what makes a chat last more than a minute.
days.challenge: Tell your yesterday in four sentences before you go to sleep.
days.mistakeWhy: After "did" the verb goes back to its base form: "I didn't go", not "I didn't went".
phrases: I had dinner with my family.
Last week I watched a film.
La semana pasada vi una película.
freeze: How do you say «…» in English?

days.title: Opinions
days.goal: Say what you think, give a reason, and agree or disagree.
days.brief: Today you give your opinion. "I think", "I agree", "It depends". With these three you can join any chat.
days.why: Giving an opinion turns you from a listener into a participant. You don't need to be right: you need to say something.
days.challenge: Give your opinion out loud on something you see today: a meal, a song, a piece of news.
days.mistakeWhy: "I am agree" doesn't exist. It's "I agree", without "am".
phrases: I think it's a good idea.
Creo que es una buena idea.
I like it because it's easy.
The beach is better than the city.
La playa es mejor que la ciudad.
La gente es muy amable aquí.
freeze: I'm not sure, but I think…
No estoy seguro, pero creo que…

days.title: Keep talking
days.can: I can keep a conversation going.
days.goal: Ask for a repeat, ask what a word means, and send the question back.
days.brief: Today you learn not to go silent. When you don't know a word, there are phrases that buy you time and keep the conversation alive.
days.why: Nobody speaks without gaps, not even in their own language. The difference is knowing what to say while you think.
days.challenge: Talk for one minute about your city. When you get stuck, use a rescue phrase and keep going.
days.mistakeWhy: "I don't know nothing" has two negatives. English needs one: "I don't know anything".
phrases: Sorry, could you say that again?
How do you say this in English?
I don't know anything about it.
Lo que quiero decir es esto.
Let me think for a second.
freeze: Let me think for a second.
It's like… how can I say it…

mistake.bad: I don't know nothing about it.
mistake.good: I don't know anything about it.

days.title: The 2-minute talk
days.can: I can talk for two minutes.
days.goal: Give a two-minute talk in four parts, with no script.
days.brief: Today is your day: two minutes speaking English. Who you are, what you like, what you did last week and why you're learning English. No script.
days.why: Comparing your Day 1 with your Day 7 is the proof that this week worked. And you keep it on record.
days.challenge: Give your 2-minute talk on your final call with Mei, and record your Day 7.
days.mistakeWhy: You don't say "explain me". It's "explain to me" or "tell me".
phrases: Today I'm going to talk about me.
Hoy voy a hablar de mí.
Primero, me gusta jugar al fútbol.
Last week I learned a lot.
Next year I'm going to travel.
El próximo año voy a viajar.
I can talk for two minutes.

library.title: Survival kit: 30 phrases so you never go blank
library.desc: The phrases that get you out of any jam. Keep them on your phone.

items: Sorry, could you say that again?
Could you speak more slowly, please?
Can you write it down, please?
How do you say «…» in English?
I don't know the word, but…
La cosa que se usa para…
Let me think for a second.

library.title: Pronunciation: 8 sounds that give away a Spanish speaker
library.desc: You don't need a perfect accent. With these eight tweaks you'll be understood much better.

tips.p: We say "espain" or "estudent". The s goes on its own: "Spain", "student". Start with a hiss: sss-pain.
Stick your tongue out a little between your teeth and blow. Like the z in Spain: "think", "thank you".
The short i (ship, live, it) is more relaxed than our i. The long one (sheep, leave, eat) is stretched.
In English the v is made with your top teeth on your bottom lip: "very", "video".
It's not silent: it's a soft breath, like a very gentle j. "hello", "house", "happy".
It almost never sounds "ed". "worked" sounds "workt", "played" sounds "pleid". Only after t or d is it "id": "wanted".
The English j sounds like a voiced, soft "ch": "job", "January". The y is like our i: "yes", "you".
One syllable sounds stronger than the rest, and if you move it, the word changes: "PHOtograph", "phoTOgraphy".

library.title: Your 30-second introduction
library.desc: A template to fill in with your life. Learn it and you'll use it forever.
template: In my free time I like ____ and ____.
En mi tiempo libre me gusta ____ y ____.

library.title: 20 questions to keep a chat alive
library.desc: When you don't know what to say, ask. People love talking about themselves.

items: How long have you lived here?
What do you do in your free time?
What kind of music do you like?
Have you seen any good films lately?
What did you do at the weekend?
Where did you go on holiday?
What's the best thing about it?

library.title: After the Sprint: your 30-day plan
library.desc: The Sprint breaks the fear. This 15-minutes-a-day plan stops it coming back.

tips.p: Repeat one Speech Mode conversation a day. The same one. When it comes out without thinking, switch to another.
Shadow your own script for 5 minutes a day. Record yourself on Sunday and compare it with your Day 7.
One real sentence in English a day: in a shop, in a comment, in a voice note to a friend.
Talk for 3 minutes in a row on a new topic every day. Use the rescue phrases when you get stuck.

library.title: The 16 typical mistakes of Spanish speakers
library.desc: "I have 25 years", "I am agree"… With the right sentence and why each one happens.
